title.narrative: Enabling Climate-Responsive Business Environment Improvement Program (Subprogram 1)

description.narrative: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has been providing support to improve the business environment and promote small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Tajikistan. Leveraging previous initiatives, the program aims to improve the overall business environment for private businesses in Tajikistan, with a particular focus on climate-friendly private businesses and SMEs.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

1.1. To foster climate-friendly investment and increase green jobs in the private sector, the MOF approved regulations through a decree to establish: (i) criteria for identifying climate-friendly SMEs;b and (ii) a policy for state-owned banks to provide subsidized financing to climate-friendly SMEs.

1.2. The MEDT operationalized a unit within the MEDT for implementing the recently approved GEDS and (i) allocated three positions for the unit, with at least one position allocated for women within the unit to promote gender diversity; and (ii) approved the workplan for the unit.

1.3. To enhance financing opportunities for the SME sector: (i) The MOF issued an order approving a policy to strengthen the leasing sector by addressing key bottlenecks such as required regulatory and taxation issues and provided criteria on climate-friendly businesses. (ii) The government increased state budget allocation for presidential grants for women-led enterprises from TJS2.5 million to TJS5.0 million, with up to 10% of this grant allocated to climate-friendly businesses.

2.1. To improve fiscal transparency and accountability, the MOF issued an order to (i) establish a dedicated unit responsible for collecting, organizing, and publishing GFS data in accordance with the GFSM 2014 framework; and (ii) mandated the quarterly publication of GFS data.

2.2. To improve infrastructure governance, ensure better infrastructure for private business and address climate change challenges, the Government of Tajikistan completed performance of the PIMA and climate PIMA to identify inefficiencies towards public investment management practices in Tajikistan.

2.3. To strengthen compliance management through the progressive implementation of risk-based approaches, the Tax Committee approved the compliance improvement plan for large taxpayers in the construction sector.

2.4. To optimize and strengthen the overall digital transformation and e-commerce in Tajikistan, the government: (i) operationalized the Agency for Innovation and Digitalization created in 2021 by appointing the Chairman of the Agency; approved regulations of the Agency indicating structure, responsibilities, and staffing; and allocated funds totaling TJS4.0 million for the agency for FY2024. (ii) approved the E-Commerce Program (2024-2028) for Tajikistan and Action Plan (2024-2026), covering (a) interagency coordination, (b) strengthening e-government services for provision of public services to the citizens, (c) legislative framework for data security and data management, (d) consumer protection, (e) intellectual property rights, (f) incentives for SMEs related to e-commerce, and (g) strengthening the capacity of women entrepreneurs though a dedicated action plan.
24 Jul 2024 | News Release: https://www.adb.org/news/50-million-adb-grant-support-climate-friendly-business-environment-tajikistan

3.1. To promote innovation and adaptation of modern technology and enhance opportunities for climate-friendly private sector investment, the amendments and additions to the Law on Technological Parks were approved by the government. The amended law provides clarity regarding (i) creation and operations of technology parks; (ii) shapes of the techno parks; and (iii) rights of nonresident foreign tenants within such parks.

3.2. To facilitate export diversification and promote climate-friendly private sector, the MOF and Export Agency, through an order, jointly approved: (i) a framework to support exporters through (a) financial incentives for climate-friendly exporters or for traditional export industries to transition to climate-friendly operations; (b) trade facilitation services through export documentation and compliance assistance; (c) creation of export acceleration program for new and existing exports to enter into foreign markets; (ii) at least 15% of the funding was allocated for women-led climate-friendly entrepreneurs involved in exports. (iii) the government allocated TJS20 million to the Agency for Export of Tajikistan to support exporters.

3.3. To enhance investment opportunities, mobilize financing for infrastructure development and climate-related initiatives, (i) the government updated regulatory framework for the issuance of local currency bond and raised TJS100 million, through issuance of local bonds; and (ii) the government updated the regulatory framework for issuance of Green Bonds during FY2024.
